note: Fourteen printables, plus 01b — an A3 alternative to the sound-frame mat, made by the same builder and by the Writing Shelf generator at /montree/library/tools/writing-shelf-generator. All adult-facing text sits outside the cards. CUT ONCE: cards butt against each other with no gutters, and every cut line runs the full width or the full height of the page, edge to edge, so one straight stroke of the blade separates the cards on both sides of it. The lines are light-grey 0.25 mm hairlines — they are cut away, so a line IS the card edge — and a small black triangle at the 5.5 mm printer-safe margin marks each line where it meets the paper edge, because a hairline dies in the last few millimetres of any printer. Card content stops 4 mm inside every card edge, so a wandering blade never touches a photograph or a word. Footer on every sheet: “Cut along every grey line · N cards”. Sheets 02, 03, 06, 13 and 14 are MOUNTED on coloured backing card with a 1 cm border, so their printed size is 20 mm smaller than the finished card; 04, 05, 09, 11 and 12 are not mounted and print at finished size. Sheet 14’s backing card is not any colour: PINK for its tier 1 cards, BLUE for its tier 2 and GREEN for its tier 3, because on that sheet the colour IS the reading level. Sheet 12’s word card is the same 60 × 35 mm as sheet 04’s heart word, set in the same face at the same size on the same baseline, so a heart word off the Tray 4 ring and a word out of the Tray 5 tin sit as one sentence on the sentence line.

items.title: Story starter cards ×14 — 80 × 120 mm
items.note: The supplement that unsticks Tray 5. A child who can read every card in the tin can still sit in front of an empty sentence line, because inventing a sentence out of nothing is a bigger leap than reading one. He pulls a card, says what he sees, builds THAT out of the tin — and then turns the card over. The back carries the one decodable sentence the picture is of, so the card corrects him itself and no adult has to be standing there. Not tied to any one lesson: it is on the tray all year. Same card as sheets 02 and 03 — 80 × 120 mm printed, mounted on coloured backing card to 100 × 140 — because these are picked up and physically TURNED, which is what a flip card is for. THE SENTENCE IS LOWER CASE and set in Comic Neue — teacher review of the printed proofs, 2026-09-12. These are the literal words a four-year-old says when he looks at the picture (“hen in a pen”, not “Hen in a pen”); the capital and the full stop are his to add with a punctuation tile off the tray. Comic Neue is the free SIL-OFL face metrically similar to Comic Sans MS, which is Microsoft-licensed and cannot be embedded in a PDF the shelf ships; adult text in the margin is still Andika. THE CARD FRAME IS NEW, and it is the whole of the second round of proofs (2026-09-12): the 1.5 mm square-cornered rule printed as a thin line floating in a large white margin — “a line someone drew” — rather than as a designed card. It is now a ROUNDED DOUBLE FRAME, identical on sheets 13 and 14 and imported constant for constant so the two decks cannot drift: 2.6 mm of stroke with a 5 mm outer corner radius, its OUTER edge 4 mm off the cut line on all four sides so the bleed the blade works into is even the whole way round, and a 0.4 mm hairline of the same colour 2.2 mm inside it, cornered to match. The double rule is the playing-card and certificate cue. Content sits 0.8 mm inside the hairline, square on all four sides, in a 60 × 100 mm box. EVERY ONE OF THE FOURTEEN IS FRAMED, on both faces. Until now exactly one card carried a rule and thirteen carried nothing, which read as an unfinished deck rather than as a highlight. “hen in a pen” keeps sheet 14’s tier-1 PINK (#D45B86, imported from the sheet 14 builder so the hex cannot drift) because it is the card the teacher starts a child on and she wants to find it in the tray by eye; the other thirteen are framed in a WARM CHARCOAL (#5A5248), a considered neutral close in temperature to the house adult-text grey, deliberately NOT a fourth reading tier beside sheet 14’s pink, blue and green, and a solid mid-dark value a school laser prints clean at 2.6 mm. THE ART IS TRIMMED TO ITS OWN INK AND FILLS THE BOX. The source drawings carry whatever white margin the generator gave them, and on the proofs that margin printed as dead space round a small subject. The builder now measures each drawing’s ink at build time — the box holding all but 0.2 % of its ink WEIGHT at each edge, so soft pencil shading and a light wash are kept while the fading tip of a ground scribble is not — crops to it, gives back an even 2 % breathing margin and fits the result into the whole 60 × 100 mm content box, aspect preserved and centred ON THE INK, which is also what fixed drawings printing low in the card. Every card reaches the full 60 mm width; a wide composition is simply shorter. The source files are never written to. ONE EM FOR BOTH DECKS. The sentence size is no longer a per-card result: 10.90 mm of em, a 7.3 mm cap height — three times the cap height of a reading book — sets every sentence on sheets 13 and 14, and a sentence of three words or fewer sets on ONE line wherever it fits at that em. The old wrap took whatever size each sentence could reach, so “the cat sat” and “the ant sat” set large on one line while “the sun sat” — the same eleven characters — broke to two and came out visibly smaller. A longer sentence takes the fewest lines that fit at that same em, so the deck steps down in line count and never in type size. Holding EVERY three-word sentence to one line without exception would peg the em to the longest of them, “the penguin spat”, at 8.4 mm — a small line of type adrift in a large white card, too timid to be read at arm’s length by the child it is for, and a waste of the frame. Letting that one card wrap to “the penguin / spat” costs one card on one green sheet and buys 30 % bigger letterforms on every other card in both decks. Six of sheet 13’s fourteen and seven of sheet 14’s eighteen take two or three lines at this em; the rest set on one, and every one of them sets at the same size.
